content:
{
  "root_cause": "The Escape key pressed on the access toggle button is always consumed by the dropdown's data API keydown handler, preventing the event from reaching the modal's keyboard dismiss listener. This causes the modal to remain open when Escape should close it (as expected by the test).",
  "repair_strategy": "Modify the dropdown's `dataApiKeydownHandler` to only prevent default and stop propagation for the Escape key when the dropdown menu is currently shown (i.e., the toggle has the 'show' class). When the menu is not shown, allow the Escape event to propagate so ancestors like the modal can handle it. Keep existing behavior for ArrowUp/Down and Space keys.",
  "expected_accessibility_effect": "Escape will now correctly dismiss the share modal when focus is on the access button and the dropdown menu is closed, restoring expected keyboard navigation behavior for modal dialogs.",
  "functional_risks": [
    "Changing Escape handling may affect components that rely on Escape to close dropdowns even when nested; however the change only allows Escape to propagate when the dropdown is not open, preserving existing behavior for open dropdowns.",
    "If a dropdown is programmatically opened without the 'show' class (unlikely), Escape might propagate unintentionally.",
    "Potential conflict with other keyboard handlers upstream if they also listen for Escape."
  ],
  "verification_requirements": [
    "Press Escape on the access button when the dropdown is closed should close the modal (or cause #access-toggle to become invisible per test).",
    "Press Escape when the dropdown is open should close only the dropdown menu and not the modal.",
    "ArrowUp/Down and Space keys should still operate as before to open the dropdown and navigate items.",
    "Ensure no regression in core dropdown functionality (opening, closing, keyboard navigation)."
  ]
}
